title: What is the area of this parallelogram after a cut and a slide?
description: A parallelogram with base nine centimetres and height five centimetres is cut along a height, and the small triangle slides across to make a rectangle. The length and breadth of that rectangle give the area. Keeko doubts this and multiplies the base by the slanting side instead of the height.
teaching_notes: One idea: cutting along a height and sliding the triangle turns a parallelogram into a rectangle with the same base and height, so area is base times height. Watch for students who multiply by the slanting side.

source: A parallelogram has base 9 cm and height 5 cm. Cut and slide
video_script.why: The child sees why the area of a parallelogram is base times height: a cut along a height and a slide make a rectangle, and nothing is lost.
video_script.substitution: Cut along the height, slide the triangle to the other end, and multiply the length and breadth of the rectangle.
video_script.anchor: the book's parallelogram ABCD with the height AX, cut and slid into a rectangle
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko multiplies the base by the slanting side, nine times six, instead of by the height.
video_script.payoff_line: The area of the parallelogram is forty five square centimetres
maths_rules: parallelogram ABCD: base DC = 9 cm, height AX = 5 cm, X on DC
the slanting side AD = 6 cm is drawn, only for Keeko's doubt; DX = square root of (36 − 25) = square root of 11, about 3.3 cm, so X lies inside DC
triangle AXD fits over triangle BYC: AX = BY, angle AXD = angle BYC = 90 degrees, AD = BC
DX = CY, so XY = XC + CY = XC + DX = DC = 9 cm
rectangle ABYX: 9 × 5 = 45 cm², the same as the parallelogram
video_script.design: One parallelogram all video: a height, a cut, a slide and a rectangle. Keeko's doubt uses the slanting side in place of the height.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='para'/>A parallelogram has a base of nine centimetres and a height of five centimetres.
<bookmark mark='cut'/>It is cut along a height, and one piece slides across to make a rectangle.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the area of the parallelogram?

beats.on_screen: the parallelogram holds still and glows

marks.stop: the parallelogram glows in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: parallelogram ABCD with the base DC at the bottom; the dotted line AX drops from A to X on DC with a right angle mark; the words height and dissection appear in turn

marks.line: a dotted line drops from the corner A straight down to the base
marks.meet: the point X and a right angle mark appear on the base DC
marks.ht: the word height is written beside AX
marks.dis: the word dissection is written, with the cut and slide shown small

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>From the top corner eigh, draw a straight line down to the base.
<bookmark mark='meet'/>It meets the base D C at a point X, at a right angle.
<bookmark mark='ht'/>We call this line eigh X a height of the parallelogram.
<bookmark mark='dis'/>Cutting a figure into pieces and joining them as another figure of equal area is called dissection.

beats.on_screen: Given: parallelogram ABCD, base DC = 9 cm, height AX = 5 cm

marks.given: the base and the height are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a parallelogram eigh B C D has a base D C of nine centimetres.
Its height eigh X is five centimetres.

beats.on_screen: To find: the area of the parallelogram

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the area of the parallelogram.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: cut along AX into the triangle AXD and the piece ABCX

marks.cut: the parallelogram is cut along eigh X into the triangle eigh X D and the piece eigh B C X

narration: <bookmark mark='cut'/>Step one, cut along the height eigh X.
This gives a triangle eigh X D and a four sided piece eigh B C X.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: slide ΔAXD to ΔBYC; AX = BY, ∠AXD = ∠BYC = 90°, AD = BC; ABYX is a rectangle

marks.slide: the triangle eigh X D slides across to the right
marks.fit: it lands exactly on the triangle B Y C
marks.eq: the equal heights eigh X and B Y and the equal slanting sides eigh D and B C are ticked
marks.rect: the rectangle eigh B Y X is outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='slide'/>Step two, slide the triangle eigh X D across to the right.
<bookmark mark='fit'/>It fits exactly over the triangle B Y C, because both have a right angle.
<bookmark mark='eq'/>The heights eigh X and B Y are equal. The slanting sides eigh D and B C are equal too.
<bookmark mark='rect'/>The piece and the triangle together make the rectangle eigh B Y X.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: breadth AX = 5; length XY = XC + CY = XC + DX = DC = 9

marks.sides: the sides of the rectangle are marked
marks.len: XY = DC = 9 is written along the length
marks.com: XC is shown added to both DX and CY

narration: <bookmark mark='sides'/>Step three, find the sides of the rectangle.
Its breadth is eigh X, five centimetres.
<bookmark mark='len'/>Its length X Y is the same as the base D C.
<bookmark mark='com'/>This is because D X and C Y are equal, and X C is added to both.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: area of a parallelogram = area of the rectangle = length × breadth = base × height = 9 × 5

marks.same: the parallelogram and the rectangle are shown with an equals sign between them
marks.rule: area of a parallelogram = base × height is written
marks.put: the numbers 9 and 5 replace base and height

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step four, the parallelogram has the same area as the rectangle.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The area of a parallelogram is its base times its height.
<bookmark mark='put'/>Here the base is nine and the height is five.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Nine times five is forty five, so the area of the parallelogram is forty five square centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the parallelogram
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble reads 9 × 6 = 54; the slanting side 6 cm leans beside the rectangle whose height is 5 cm; the bubble is struck out

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble appears with the slanting side of 6 cm
marks.lean: the slanting side leans and is drawn longer than the height
marks.high: the rectangle's height of 5 cm is marked
marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and base × height is written

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the area is fifty four square centimetres, using the slanting side of six centimetres.
<bookmark mark='lean'/>But the slanting side leans over, so it is longer than the height.
<bookmark mark='high'/>The rectangle we made is only five centimetres high.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The height meets the base at a right angle, and the base is multiplied by it.
